shock.note: The Fed stopping after December (or reversing) by April has two causes with opposite effects on stocks: inflation cooling fast as oil falls (S&P up a few percent), or growth and markets cracking (S&P down around 10%). Kalshi prices a cut before July 2027 near 45%, which says the second is live. I weight them about evenly and put the S&P 1% below the baseline; the sign is the least certain figure in this row.
Long yields fall in both versions: about 0.15 points if inflation cools, more if growth cracks. The reverse of the +0.12 points seen when one extra rise was priced, scaled up for the stress case.
The dollar's 19-month high rests on the rate gap; a Fed that stops gives back about what it gained when one rise was priced.
The mirror of BND's 1.7% fall when one extra rise was priced: one or more rises fewer than the baseline.

worst_outcome.title: The Fed's rate is 5.00% or higher after April: a rise at every meeting, or a half-point step
